newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish industrialists say 1997 budget unrealistic.
newsitem.headline: Turkish industrialists say 1997 budget unrealistic.

text.p: Turkish industrialists said on Wednesday a sharp increase foreseen in non-tax revenues under the Islamist-led government's 1997 draft zero-deficit budget was an unrealistic target.
"Budget figures raise concerns among the industrialists. It is not concrete enough," said Husamettin Kavi, chairman of the Istanbul Chamber of Industry (ISO).

Speaking at an ISO meeting, Kavi said the 1997 draft budget, submitted to parliament last week, proposed a 765 percent increase in non-tax earnings in expectation that $3.5 billion of it would come from the sale of a 20 percent stake in Turk Telekom, Turkey's state-owned telecommunications giant.
"About 1,500 trillion lira of non-tax income is not realistic," he said.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan described his $46.3 billion draft budget as a revolution in the 73-year history of the Turkish republic.
The 1997 budget predicts tax earnings at 4,368 trillion lira, up 98.5 percent from the 1996 target.
Non-tax earnings are targeted at 1,445 trillion lira.

Memduh Hacioglu, an industrialist and former ISO chairman, said the government could not attain its zero deficit target unless it "launches a massive privatisation drive, cancels debt servicing, and tighten its expenditures."

"Politicians do not have rights for unlimited spending, printing money, borrowing and introducing new taxes according to their own wishes. If we want a reliable government, they should discipline themselves," he said.
On the expenditure side, the government targets to keep spending at 6,255 trillion lira, up from the 1996 target of 3,946 trillion.

Mesut Yilmaz, leader of the main-opposition Motherland Party, predicted the 1997 budget deficit at 2,200 trillion lira. The 1996 deficit is expected to overshoot to 1,300 trillion lira against an initial target of 861 trillion.

"There is an exaggeration of 1,100 trillion lira in the non-tax revenue target. Interest payments will overshoot the target by 936 trillion and deficits of social security institutions and state economic enterprises by 250 trillion," Yilmaz told his deputies at a meeting on Wednesday.

Halit Narin, a textile and tourism industrialist, described the zero-deficit target only as a slogan for the ruling Islamist Welfare Party and its junior conservative coalition partner True Path Party.
